blurb: `withHeader` adds a header of the handler's own, so it cannot set one the router writes itself: the caching headers (`Cache-Control`, `ETag`, `Vary`), `Content-Type` and `Content-Length`, `Location`, `Set-Cookie`, the `security { }` headers, the `Access-Control-*` CORS headers, `WWW-Authenticate` and `Allow`, and the hop-by-hop headers. Each has its own way in: `@cache`, a body, `.at(url)`, `withCookie`, `security { }`, `cors { }`. A name computed at run time is checked when the response is built, and a reserved one answers `500`. See also `bynk.http.invalid_response_header`.
summary: `withHeader` names a header the router owns, such as `Set-Cookie`, `Cache-Control` or `Location`.
